answers.children: Yes — Spanish Water Dogs get along well with children when the youngsters respect their space. Their herding instinct leads them to gently guide toddlers away from trouble, yet the breed’s high energy and medium build mean an excited burst can knock over a small child. The curly coat and loyal nature make them attentive around the family they bond with strongly. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Spanish Water Dogs can get along with other pets if raised together. Their working background as herders gives them a drive to organise rather than chase, though the same-sex tension and wariness of strangers can create friction with unfamiliar dogs. Loyal and intelligent, they form strong bonds with household animals when exercise and training channel their energetic temperament.
answers.exercise: Spanish Water Dogs need 60 to 90 minutes of vigorous daily exercise. Without it their boundless energy turns into unraveled garden hoses and restless circling; long hikes, lake swims and intense fetch sessions suit their history of herding livestock and retrieving from water. The curly-coated breed thrives when both body and mind stay occupied.
answers.shedding: No — Spanish Water Dogs shed lightly year-round. Their medium curly coat lacks the heavy undercoat of many working breeds, so loose hair stays trapped in the woolly texture rather than spreading across floors, yet the curls still require regular attention to prevent matting in a rustic powerhouse built for marshland work.
answers.hypoallergenic: The Spanish Water Dog has a medium curly coat that sheds lightly and produces minimal loose hair around the house. The tight curls trap much of the dander and dead hair so it does not spread as freely as in straight-coated breeds, yet the coat still requires regular grooming to prevent matting. No breed is genuinely hypoallergenic and the Spanish Water Dog is not among those usually suggested to allergy sufferers.
answers.training: Yes — Spanish Water Dogs are easy to train. Their high intelligence and biddability, paired with an original purpose herding livestock and retrieving in water without constant direction, make them quick to learn when given clear tasks, though their energetic drive requires consistent work to prevent boredom-induced mischief.
answers.lifespan: Spanish Water Dogs live 12-14 years. Their rustic build and history as versatile workers on the Iberian Peninsula support a solid robustness that holds up to demanding activity, yet the high exercise needs and energetic temperament mean a lifestyle matching their boundless drive helps them stay fit across that range.
answers.size: Spanish Water Dogs reach 31-49 lb and stand 16-20 in at the shoulder. The medium, compact and sturdy frame feels like a compact bundle of power in the home, substantial enough to dive through icy ponds or herd with grit but not so large that the loyal, curly-coated dog overwhelms a family living space.
answers.barking: Spanish Water Dogs bark moderately. Bred to alert while herding sheep and assisting fishermen, they issue a sharp bark or two at strangers or unusual activity rather than constant noise, their intelligent and loyal nature directing vocalisation toward guarding the strong family bond instead of random sounds.
answers.apartment: No — Spanish Water Dogs do not suit apartment living. Their high exercise needs, energetic drive and tendency toward mischief when under-stimulated clash with confined indoor settling, while the medium curly coat and wariness of strangers add to the challenge of meeting the demands of this versatile working breed.
answers.first-time: No — Spanish Water Dogs are not a good first dog. The high exercise needs and strong-willed intelligence demand an owner who can match their versatile working drive and channel loyalty into structured activity, or the energetic curly-coated breed will quickly outpace a novice with restless behaviour and wariness toward strangers.
